quandoUsar: An agent proposes an action with a real effect (refund, send, delete) and a person must approve or reject it before it happens.
Requests that need context: a summary, facts as label and value pairs and, optionally, a preview of the change behind the details button.
Review queues where the card stays on screen after the decision, showing what was decided and an “Undo”.
quandoEvitar: Use `tool-approval` for a compact request inside the conversation, with allow once, allow always or deny.
Use `confirm-morph` or `hold-to-confirm` when the person themselves triggers a destructive action and only needs to confirm it.
Use `dialog` when the decision must block the rest of the screen until it is made.

teclado.acao: Activates the focused button: details, reject, approve or undo.
Moves through the controls in DOM order: details button, reject and approve.

acessibilidade: The root is a `<section>` labeled by `title`; the details button exposes `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and the result appears in a `role="status"` region.
On decision, the pressed button leaves the DOM and the code does not move focus, which lands on `body`; if the queue is used by keyboard, move focus yourself in `onStatusChange`.
“Show details”, “Hide details”, “Undo” and “needs your approval” are fixed in English; only `approveLabel`, `rejectLabel` and `resolvedLabels` can be translated.
movimento: On decision, the icon becomes a check mark or an X that draws itself, a ripple leaves the badge and the buttons give way to the result with a short fade.
The details open with a height spring and the fact rows enter in sequence.
With “reduce motion” on, only opacity changes remain: no ripple, no stroke drawing and no color or scale transitions.
responsivo: When the window is up to 26rem wide (media query, not container), the two buttons split the full row; the card always fills 100% of the parent.
notasIA: The card only records the decision: run the action in `onStatusChange` and, to reflect what the server replied, control `status` (`pending`, `approved`, `rejected`).
“Undo” returns the card to `pending` and calls `onStatusChange("pending")`; if the action cannot be undone once executed, pass `allowUndo={false}`.
The details button only appears when there are `details` or `children`; each `label` in `details` is used as the `key`, so do not repeat labels.
